releases.title: Invite a classmate
releases.intro: Studying is easier with a friend.

highlights.title: A ready-made invite
highlights.text: On any class page, or in a study group, tap Invite. A short message is ready to share, copy or text, and you can change it first.

highlights.title: Just a friendly invite
highlights.text: Nothing is sent for you, and nobody earns anything for inviting.

releases.title: Report anything shared
releases.intro: Keeping shared study sets kind and useful.

highlights.title: A report button on everything shared
highlights.text: Something in a group or a shared link not okay? Report it in two taps. Reports are private.

highlights.title: Hidden fast
highlights.text: When three different students report the same thing, it's hidden right away until a person takes a look.

highlights.title: Group owners can act
highlights.text: Owners can still take things down at any time, and bring back something that was hidden by mistake.

releases.title: Edit together
releases.intro: Make a group's study set better, together.

highlights.title: Everyone can improve it
highlights.text: In a study group, open a shared set to fix a card or improve a note section. The change shows up for everyone in the group.

highlights.title: Every change, with a name
highlights.text: See who changed what and when, and undo any change. An undo never wipes out someone's newer edit.

highlights.title: Lock it when it's right
highlights.text: Whoever shared the set, or the group's owner, can lock it so only the sharer can edit.

releases.title: Study groups
releases.intro: Study with a few classmates, without the group chat noise.

highlights.title: Invite only
highlights.text: Start a group and invite classmates with a code or link, up to 40 people. Members see first names only. There's no chat.

highlights.title: A shared library
highlights.text: Share your study sets with the group. Anyone in it can add their own copy to their class.

highlights.title: You're in control
highlights.text: Leave any time; what you shared leaves with you. The owner can remove people, take sets down and make a new code.

releases.title: Share a study set
releases.intro: Made a great study set? Send it to a classmate.

highlights.title: A private link
highlights.text: On a file's page, tap Share. The link works only for students signed in to Stoga.study, lasts 30 days, and you can turn it off any time.

highlights.title: Add to my class
highlights.text: Opening a link shows what's in the set. Add it and you get your own copy of the notes, flashcards, quizzes and guide, with cards starting fresh.

highlights.title: Private by design
highlights.text: Only the study set is shared. Your own notes, progress and mistakes never are, and nothing anyone does with their copy comes back to you.

releases.title: Easier for everyone
releases.intro: An accessibility pass across the app, and a switch for motion.

highlights.title: Checked screen by screen
highlights.text: Every main screen was checked for screen readers, keyboard use and contrast, in light and dark.

highlights.title: Reduce motion
highlights.text: Settings, Display has a Motion switch that turns off animations in the app, even if your device allows them.

releases.title: Keyboard shortcuts
releases.intro: Study faster from a laptop.

highlights.title: Quizzes and tests
highlights.text: A to D picks an answer, Enter checks it and moves on, H shows a hint. In practice tests, arrow keys move between questions.

highlights.title: Get around
highlights.text: Press / to search, and G then a letter to jump: G H for Home, G C for Calendar, G R for Review, G O for your coach.

highlights.title: See them all
highlights.text: Press ? anywhere for the full list.

releases.title: Install it like an app
releases.intro: Stoga.study on your Home Screen, one tap away.

highlights.title: One-tap install
highlights.text: On Chrome, Edge and Android, install Stoga.study from Home or Settings. It opens like an app and works offline.

highlights.title: iPhone steps
highlights.text: On iPhone and iPad, a short guide shows you how to add it to your Home Screen, which also turns on reminders.

releases.title: Pick up on any device
releases.intro: Start on your laptop, keep going on your phone.

highlights.title: Continue studying, everywhere
highlights.text: Home offers the last file, note or review you had open, even if it was on another device.

highlights.title: Your coach chat follows you
highlights.text: Your conversation with your coach shows up on your phone and your laptop.

releases.title: Quizzes offline, too
releases.intro: On the bus or somewhere without Wi-Fi? Keep studying.

highlights.title: Take quizzes offline
highlights.text: Answer practice quizzes with no connection. Your answers, score and mistakes sync on their own when you're back online.

highlights.title: Ready before you need it
highlights.text: Your recent quizzes and study sets are saved on your device ahead of time, so they open even offline.

releases.title: Sturdier on a shaky connection
releases.intro: Fewer dead ends when the Wi-Fi drops or a server has a moment.

highlights.title: It tries again by itself
highlights.text: Loading, saving an upload and the coach all retry on their own after a passing hiccup, instead of showing an error.

highlights.title: Smoother updates
highlights.text: The update notice says what's new and links to it. Screens that changed in an update reload themselves instead of showing a problem.

highlights.title: Tell us in one tap
highlights.text: If a screen does hit a problem, Send a report tells us what went wrong, so we can fix it fast.

releases.title: Check-ins from your coach
releases.intro: Your coach can now reach out, now and then, when it matters.

highlights.title: When it helps
highlights.text: After a rough quiz, when a test is close and you've been away a couple of days (“Your Bio test is Friday: 10 minutes tonight?”), or after a quiet stretch.

highlights.title: Never pushy
highlights.text: Still one notification an evening at most, each kind at most weekly, different words each time, and its own switch in Settings.

releases.title: Gentle reminders
releases.intro: Optional phone notifications that respect your evenings.

highlights.title: At most one a day
highlights.text: An evening nudge only if you have cards due and haven't studied yet, and a heads-up the night before a test. Each has its own switch.

highlights.title: Your times, your quiet hours
highlights.text: Pick when reminders come and when they never do. Nothing is sent during quiet hours.

highlights.title: iPhone too
highlights.text: Add Stoga.study to your Home Screen, then turn on reminders in Settings. There's a step-by-step guide.

releases.title: Quiet milestones
releases.intro: A few moments worth marking, without the noise.

highlights.title: Moments that matter
highlights.text: Your first review, 100 cards learned, your first unit mastered, four weeks in a row, 90% on a practice test and a few more. Each one shows up once on Home, then lives on your Progress page.

highlights.title: No points, no leaderboards
highlights.text: Just you and how far you've come.

releases.title: Streaks, your way
releases.intro: An optional weekly streak that works around your life.

highlights.title: Pick your days
highlights.text: Choose how many days a week you want to study, from 1 to 7. Hit that and the week counts. The rest are rest days.

highlights.title: No guilt
highlights.text: A week you can't make just doesn't count, and that's okay. Going away or sick? Pause the week and your streak is safe. Always free.

highlights.title: Only real studying counts
highlights.text: Reviewing cards, quizzes, practice tests and asking the tutor. Turn it on from Progress.

releases.title: Goals, and your week in review
releases.intro: Set a weekly goal that fits you, and look back on each week.

highlights.title: Weekly goals
highlights.text: Up to four: study days, cards reviewed, quiz questions or study minutes, for all classes or one. Or make your own, like “Read a chapter”, and tick it off. They reset every week.

highlights.title: Your week in review
highlights.text: At the start of each week: what you studied, your best day, which class picked up, how your goals went, and one thing to try next.

releases.title: See how you're really doing
releases.intro: Progress now shows your study history, how consistent you are, and where each class is heading.

highlights.title: Study history
highlights.text: A heatmap of the last 20 weeks: every day you reviewed cards, answered quiz questions, took a practice test or asked the tutor. Tap a day to see what you did.

highlights.title: Trends
highlights.text: Your card recall and quiz accuracy, week by week.

highlights.title: By class
highlights.text: How much you studied each class in the last 30 days compared with the 30 before, with recall, quiz scores and mastery.

highlights.title: Sessions
highlights.text: Your recent study sessions: when, which classes, what you did and how it went.

releases.title: Faces, redrawn
releases.intro: Faces are now black-and-white ink drawings, cleaner and more grown-up.

highlights.title: A new look
highlights.text: Bold ink lines, solid black hair and small, expressive features. Pick a background color and clothes (tee, black tee, collar, hoodie or stripes). Your old face carries over.

releases.title: Dates your way
releases.intro: Dates and times now follow your language and region.

highlights.title: Your format
highlights.text: Day and month names, 12 or 24-hour time, and whether weeks start on Sunday or Monday all match where you are, everywhere in the app.

highlights.title: Pick a language
highlights.text: In Settings, Display, choose from 16 languages. “Tomorrow” becomes “Mañana”, “Demain” or “明天”, and your coach replies in that language too.

releases.title: Faces, and a coach that's yours
releases.intro: Give your coach a face, a name and a personality. You get a face too.

highlights.title: Build a face
highlights.text: Pick the head shape, skin, hair and hair color, eyes, brows, mouth, extras like glasses or headphones, and colors. Or hit Shuffle.

highlights.title: It comes alive
highlights.text: Your coach blinks, glances around while it thinks, and talks while it answers.

highlights.title: Name and personality
highlights.text: Call it whatever you like, and pick how it talks: Chill, Hype, Straight up or Calm, with short, normal or detailed replies.

highlights.title: Your face, too
highlights.text: Make your own in Settings. It shows at the top of the app.

releases.title: A much smarter coach
releases.intro: The coach can now see your study material and do real things with it.

highlights.title: It knows your stuff
highlights.text: It can search and read your notes and files, check how you're doing in each class, go through your quiz mistakes and find your hardest cards, then answer with real numbers.

highlights.title: It does things
highlights.text: Ask for flashcards from your latest notes, a study plan written into your notes, or a test added to your calendar. Every change has an Undo button, and it can't delete your study material.

highlights.title: Buttons to jump in
highlights.text: When it helps, it gives you a button to start a review, a practice test, a unit quiz or open a file.

highlights.title: Feels alive
highlights.text: Watch it work step by step, then read its answer as it streams in. Stop it any time.

releases.title: Smarter calendar imports
releases.intro: Imported items land in the right place more often.

highlights.title: Knows school words
highlights.text: Presentations, DBQs, summatives, check-ins, DeltaMath and more. Test reviews and corrections count as homework, not the test.

highlights.title: Knows your classes' nicknames
highlights.text: Chem, APUSH, Calc, Precalc and others match the right class.

highlights.title: AI for the rest
highlights.text: Anything still unsure gets a quick AI look, so “EME Presentations” lands in World History. Anything you've already changed stays as you set it.

releases.title: Bring your own calendar
releases.intro: Already keep your assignments somewhere? Bring them in.

highlights.title: Import a calendar
highlights.text: On the Calendar, tap Import. Paste a calendar link from Schoology, Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar, or upload an .ics file.

highlights.title: You check it first
highlights.text: We guess whether each item is a test, quiz, homework or project, and which class it's for. Fix anything before it's added.

highlights.title: Stays in sync
highlights.text: A linked calendar updates when you open your calendar, without making copies. Your own changes and ticks stay put.

releases.title: Everything for one test, in one place
releases.intro: Tap a test on your calendar to open its own prep page.

highlights.title: Exam prep page
highlights.text: The countdown, how ready you are for each unit, your plan for it, practice tests and their scores, all on one page.

highlights.title: Review pack
highlights.text: A one-page cram sheet: the key terms, the quiz questions you missed with their answers, and the 20 cards that have been hardest for you. Print it or save it as a PDF.

releases.title: Practice tests, timed
releases.intro: Try a test under real conditions before the real one.

highlights.title: Like the real thing
highlights.text: A timer, no hints, and a mix of multiple choice and written answers. AP classes get more written questions, like the free-response section.

highlights.title: Aimed at your weak spots
highlights.text: Questions you got wrong before and your weakest cards come up first.

highlights.title: A full review after
highlights.text: Your score, every question with the right answer, and feedback on what you wrote. Misses go to mistake review and back into your cards.

highlights.title: Right from your calendar
highlights.text: Tap Take a practice test on your next test's countdown, or find it on a class page.

releases.title: The coach, on Home
releases.intro: A quick heads-up about what's coming, and one tap to plan for it.

highlights.title: A nudge that fits your week
highlights.text: Like “Biology Unit 4 test in 3 days, and 10 of its 20 cards are still new. Want tonight's plan?” Tap it and the coach picks up from there.

highlights.title: Catching up, not guilt
highlights.text: Homework past due? It offers to help you sort out when to get it done. Nothing more.

releases.title: Meet your coach
releases.intro: Someone in your corner for the planning side of school.

highlights.title: Just tell it
highlights.text: Say “bio test friday on unit 4” and it's on your calendar, with the unit. It can also move things, tick off homework, remove things and set the unit a class is on.

highlights.title: Undo, always
highlights.text: Every change shows up as a card with an Undo button, so nothing happens behind your back.

highlights.title: Real talk when it's a lot
highlights.text: Stressed about a test? It gets it, and helps you pick one small thing to do next. It counts toward your daily tutor messages.

releases.title: How ready am I?
releases.intro: Every test on your calendar now tells you how ready you are, and the one thing that would help most.

highlights.title: Ready, Getting there or Needs work
highlights.text: From how many of the test's cards you've studied, how well they're sticking, your practice quiz scores and mistakes left.

highlights.title: Unit by unit
highlights.text: A test that covers several units shows each one, so you know where to spend your time.

highlights.title: Always with a reason
highlights.text: Like “6 cards not studied yet” or “No practice quiz taken yet”. No mystery scores.

releases.title: A plan for every test
releases.intro: Add a test to your calendar and Stoga spreads the studying over the days you have.

highlights.title: Study plan
highlights.text: For each test or quiz in the next two weeks: cards from its units each day, practice quizzes, your quiz mistakes and study guides to read. A bit more in the last two days.

highlights.title: Today's plan on Home
highlights.text: Today's tasks and homework due soon, at the top of Home. Tasks tick themselves off as you review cards and finish quizzes, or tick them yourself.

highlights.title: Your time, your call
highlights.text: Pick 15, 30, 45 or 60 minutes a day on the calendar's Study plan tab. The plan fits into it.

releases.title: Your calendar
releases.intro: Keep every test, quiz and assignment in one place, next to what you study.

highlights.title: Calendar tab
highlights.text: Add tests, quizzes, homework, projects and anything else, by class. See them as a list of what's coming or as a month.

highlights.title: Homework checklist
highlights.text: Tick homework and projects off as you finish them. Anything past due and not done waits under Still to do.

highlights.title: Countdown to your next test
highlights.text: The calendar counts down to your next test or quiz. Add the units it covers, and the planner coming next will use them.

highlights.title: Coming up, on each class
highlights.text: Every class page shows its next few tests and assignments. On phones, Progress is now the chart button at the top.

releases.title: Tidy up your files
releases.intro: Keep a class neat as the year goes on, without losing anything.

highlights.title: Tags on files
highlights.text: Add tags like #lab or #test-review on any file's page. On the class page, tap a tag to see just those files.

highlights.title: Archive
highlights.text: Done with a file or a class? Archive it. Its cards and quizzes leave review, search and the tutor, and you can restore it any time from the class page.

highlights.title: Duplicate
highlights.text: Copy a file and everything made from it into the same class or another one. The copy's cards start fresh.

releases.title: Bring your cards with you
releases.intro: Already made flashcards somewhere else? Bring them in all at once.

highlights.title: Import cards
highlights.text: On a class's Flashcards page, tap Import. Paste one card per line (term - definition), or choose a CSV, a Quizlet export or an Anki export. You see what will come in before anything is added.

releases.title: Slides, too
releases.intro: Upload your teacher's slide deck and study from it like any other file.

highlights.title: PowerPoint and Google Slides
highlights.text: Upload a .pptx (in Google Slides: File, then Download, then Microsoft PowerPoint). Each slide becomes its own page, and citations say which slide.

highlights.title: Speaker notes included
highlights.text: Whatever your teacher wrote in the speaker notes comes along with each slide, so it shows up in your notes, cards and the tutor.

releases.title: Several photos, one file
releases.intro: Snap every page of your notes, then check we read them right.

highlights.title: Add several photos at once
highlights.text: Pick a few photos of your notes and they become one file, a page each, just like a PDF.

highlights.title: Check the reading
highlights.text: Before anything is saved, see what we read from each photo. Rotate a sideways one, read it again, or remove it.

highlights.title: Paste a screenshot
highlights.text: On the Upload page, paste a screenshot and it goes straight into the same check.

releases.title: Better PDF reading
releases.intro: Two fixes to how we read a PDF, so what we read matches what you see.

highlights.title: Two-column pages read in order
highlights.text: A worksheet or article printed in two columns now reads left column, then right, instead of jumbling both together line by line.

highlights.title: A scanned page inside a text PDF
highlights.text: If just a page or two of an otherwise normal PDF is a photo (a signed form, a diagram), those pages are now read too, instead of being skipped.

releases.title: See the real page
releases.intro: A citation is only as good as how easy it is to check.

highlights.title: The original file, in the app
highlights.text: Tap a page chip or a tutor citation to see the real page, jumped straight to it, with the cited passage highlighted in what we read from it. No more opening a download.

releases.title: Search everything
releases.intro: One bar for anything you've got: files, pages, your own notes, cards and quiz questions.

highlights.title: Search
highlights.text: Find a file, a page, a note you wrote, a flashcard or a quiz question, all from one search bar. Tap the search icon at the top of the app.

releases.title: AI help for your own notes
releases.intro: Your own notes, now with three AI helpers. v1.2 is complete.

highlights.title: Tidy
highlights.text: Cleans up structure, grammar and formatting, keeping everything you wrote. Review it before it replaces your note.

highlights.title: Fill gaps from the file
highlights.text: Finds facts the file covers that your notes do not mention yet, each with the page it came from, ready to add.

highlights.title: Make cards from my notes
highlights.text: Turns what you wrote into real flashcards in one tap.

releases.title: Ask about just one file or unit
releases.intro: A chat can now stay on topic, and it reads your own notes too.

highlights.title: Ask about this file, or this unit
highlights.text: From a file's page or a unit on your class page, start a conversation scoped to just that, so answers and citations stay on topic.

highlights.title: The tutor reads your own notes
highlights.text: Answers can now cite what you wrote yourself, labelled "your notes", alongside your uploaded files.

releases.title: Summaries, key terms and a focused guide
releases.intro: Two new things to make from a file, and a way to steer your study guide.

highlights.title: Summary
highlights.text: A short overview of the whole file, choosable on upload like notes or flashcards. Good for a quick refresher before diving into the details.

highlights.title: Key terms
highlights.text: A glossary of the words that matter, each with a clear definition and a page chip back to where it came from.

highlights.title: Regenerate the guide with a focus
highlights.text: On the Guide tab, tell it what to focus on, like "the midterm" or "shorter", and it remakes the guide around that.

releases.title: Worked examples and one more like it
releases.intro: Sometimes you need to see one done, or just one more rep.

highlights.title: Show a worked example
highlights.text: Stuck on a problem in the tutor? Show a worked example solves a similar one step by step, with different numbers, so yours is still yours to finish.

highlights.title: Give me one like this
highlights.text: After you check a short-answer card, ask for one more like it. A fresh variant drops in next, ready to type an answer to.

releases.title: Simpler, or go deeper
releases.intro: An answer is not always pitched right the first time. Now you can adjust it.

highlights.title: Simpler and Go deeper
highlights.text: On an explanation, or once a hint reaches the full answer, ask for it simpler or with more depth. It re-answers the same question, styled differently.

highlights.title: A default in Settings
highlights.text: Set how deep the tutor goes by default, from Simple to Deep, under AI tutor in Settings.

releases.title: Explain this
releases.intro: A confusing card or a quiz question you missed can now explain itself.

highlights.title: Explain this
highlights.text: On a card back and on a quiz question you got wrong, tap Explain this to open the tutor already talking about that exact item, grounded in the page it came from.

highlights.title: Tap a page chip
highlights.text: After you see a card's answer or a quiz question's explanation, tap its page chip for the exact sentence it came from, and a link to open the page.

releases.title: Report anything wrong
releases.intro: AI is not perfect. Now you can flag it, and it is checked before it even reaches you.

highlights.title: Something wrong here?
highlights.text: On any card, quiz question, note, study guide section or tutor answer, flag it. Cards, questions, notes and guide sections hide right away.

highlights.title: Fact-checked before you see it
highlights.text: New flashcards and quiz questions are now checked against the page they cite, and ones that are not actually supported are dropped automatically.

releases.title: See what you know
releases.intro: Mastery for every unit, whole-unit practice, and a clear next step after each session.

highlights.title: Mastery
highlights.text: Each class and unit shows Just started, Getting there or Mastered, from how well your cards stick and your latest quiz scores. See them all on Progress.

highlights.title: Practise this unit
highlights.text: A mixed quiz from every file in a unit, with questions you missed before coming first. Find it next to each unit on the class page.

highlights.title: Better summaries
highlights.text: After a review or a quiz you see what did not stick yet, your weak topics, and one next step.

releases.title: Short-answer practice
releases.intro: Writing an answer out is one of the best ways to remember it. Now you can, with any of your cards.

highlights.title: Type your answers
highlights.text: Pick a class or a deck from Review, or tap Type answers. Cards that are due come first, then weak ones.

highlights.title: The AI checks them
highlights.text: You get Right, Partly right or Not yet, what was missing, and the page it came from. Spelling slips and your own wording are fine.

highlights.title: Or check them yourself
highlights.text: Switch to I check to see the answer and grade yourself. If the AI got it wrong, tap I was right.

highlights.title: It counts as review
highlights.text: A card that is due today counts as reviewed, so you do not have to do it twice.

releases.title: Organise your cards
releases.intro: Find any card, tag it, and build your own decks.

highlights.title: Browse every card
highlights.text: Tap Browse cards on a class. Cards are sorted by unit and file. Search them, or type #tag. Tap a card to edit it.

highlights.title: Tags
highlights.text: Tag cards like #vocab or #dates, then filter by a tag in one tap.

highlights.title: Your own decks
highlights.text: Mix cards from any class into a deck, like Midterm review. Review what is due, or practise the whole deck any time. Merge decks when you are done.

highlights.title: Select many at once
highlights.text: Tap Select to tag, add to a deck, move to another class, or delete lots of cards together. You can also write your own cards.

fixes: Keep going never repeats a card you just did, even in weak-card practice.

releases.title: Smarter review
releases.intro: Shorter sessions, one unit at a time, and a way back to whatever you were doing.

highlights.title: Continue studying
highlights.text: Home picks up where you left off: a quiz you did not finish (on any device), or the note, file or review you had open.

highlights.title: Review just this unit
highlights.text: On Review, each class offers This unit or Everything. Choose 10 cards, 20 cards or all of them per session, then Keep going if you want more.

highlights.title: Weak cards
highlights.text: Cards you have missed twice, or find hard, get their own practice session. Use it any time, not just when they are due.

highlights.title: Choose how much to remember
highlights.text: In Settings: Lighter, Balanced or Thorough. Thorough brings cards back sooner, which is great before a big test.

fixes: Starting a second review in one visit could show cards you had just reviewed. It no longer does.
Updates now install by themselves the next time you switch away from the app, so you always have the latest fixes.

releases.title: Write your own notes
releases.intro: Your notes, in your words, right next to your files.

highlights.title: Notes in every class
highlights.text: Tap Write notes on a class or a file. Write as many as you like, and file each one under a unit.

highlights.title: Your file beside you
highlights.text: Notes written from a file keep it open next to them on a laptop, or one tap away on your phone.

highlights.title: Headings, bold, lists and checklists
highlights.text: Use the toolbar, or the math button for symbols like x̄, π and ≤. Tap Preview to see it tidy, and tick off checklist items.

highlights.title: Saves as you type, even offline
highlights.text: Everything is kept on your device first and syncs when you are back online.

releases.title: Your files, sorted by unit
releases.intro: Stoga now knows which unit each file belongs to, and which unit your class is on.

highlights.title: Units found for you
highlights.text: Names like Unit 11.1, U2L6 or Chapter 7 are spotted when you upload. Check it and tap Change if it is wrong. If a file does not say, we ask.

highlights.title: Classes grouped by unit
highlights.text: Each class lists its files by unit, in lesson order. Tap the pencil to name a unit.

highlights.title: Now studying
highlights.text: Your class follows the unit of your newest upload. Pin a unit to keep it there.

fixes: Files you added before this update have no unit yet. Open one and tap Change to file it.

releases.title: You choose what gets made
releases.intro: Uploading no longer makes everything automatically. You pick what you need, and how much.

highlights.title: Pick what to make
highlights.text: After you add a file, choose notes, flashcards, a practice quiz or a study guide. Or just save it to read and write your own notes.

highlights.title: Set how many
highlights.text: Choose exactly how many flashcards, quiz questions or guide sections you want. We suggest a number that fits each file.

highlights.title: Make more later
highlights.text: On any file: more flashcards, another practice quiz, or fresh notes. Everything you already have stays.

highlights.title: Saving is free
highlights.text: Only making a study set counts toward your 10 a month. Saving files never does.

highlights.title: Scans and photos
highlights.text: Scanned PDFs and photos of your notes are read now, handwriting and math included. Try Take a photo on the Upload page.

fixes: Classes that listed the same level twice (like Accelerated Literary Foundations) now show it once.
Your own API key can be from any OpenAI-compatible provider, not just OpenAI.
